headline: Israeli Shekel Drops to Over One-Year Low Against US Dollar and Euro
summary: The Israeli shekel continued to decline on Thursday, with the US dollar rising past 3.30 shekels and the euro surging to a one-year peak of 3.62 shekels.
why: Currency fluctuations in Israel reflect domestic risk premiums, institutional capital movements, and foreign exchange interventions by the Bank of Israel.

impacts.name: Israeli Shekel
impacts.why: Sustained capital outflows pushed the shekel down against major reserve currencies.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Continued selling pressures led the shekel to hit its lowest exchange value against the US dollar in over twelve months.
